THE MAKER / FRANK GATTO

A life
in guitars.

The player behind
the name on the headstock.

CHICAGO’S SOUTH SUBURBS

Music first.
Always.

Frank started guitar lessons at age 11 in Tinley Park. By 15 he was working in the music shop; at 16 he began teaching. Playing, repairs, and helping other musicians became parts of the same life.

That connection continues at Down Home Guitars in Frankfort, where he works as a teacher and repairman. He currently plays guitar with The Usual Suspects ↗.

His Down Home biography describes more than 35 years of professional playing and teaching, spanning blues, country, rock, and jazz. That experience also finds its way into the electric guitars he builds under the Gatto name.

A PLAYER’S ADVICE

“Make the other people you play with sound better.”

FRANK GATTO — Down Home Guitars

GATTO GUITARS / IN PRINT

Character in the wood.

A 2017 Down Home newsletter featured Frank’s electric guitars and noted that he had been building under his own name for six years. It described varied woods, shapes, finishes, and pickup systems—a range visible throughout the archive.

That suggests a start around 2011, although the exact founding date still needs Frank’s confirmation.
